tasks.description: Build the complete Hangman game from scratch. Pick a random word from a list, let the player guess letters, give 6 tries, show the blank display each round, and announce win or loss.
tasks.hint:
Break it into steps: 1) Pick random word with `random.choice()`, 2) `guessed = set()`, 3) Main loop with `while tries > 0 and not all_guessed`.
Display: `' '.join(c if c in guessed else '_' for c in word)`
Check each guess: if in word → show it, if not → reduce tries.
tasks.walkthrough:
This is the full game in about twenty lines. The two small helper functions keep the loop body readable.
Each round: show the blanks and tries, read a letter, record it, count it as wrong if needed.
After the loop, `won()` decides the ending message.

tasks.description: Improve your game: add input validation (only accept single letters), handle already-guessed letters, and show which letters have been guessed.
tasks.hint:
Validation: `if len(guess) != 1 or not guess.isalpha(): continue`
Already guessed: `if guess in guessed: print('Already tried!'); continue`
Show guessed letters: `print(f'Guessed: {sorted(guessed)}')` at the start of each round.
tasks.walkthrough:
Two `if ... continue` checks guard the input: one for shape (a single letter) and one for repeats.
`sorted(guessed)` shows the letters tried so far in a stable order, which is friendlier than printing the raw set.

tasks.description: Wrap the entire game in a play_hangman() function. After the game ends, ask if the player wants to play again. Loop until they say no.
tasks.hint:
`def play_hangman(): # all game logic here`
After calling it: `while input('Play again? (y/n): ').lower() == 'y': play_hangman()`
Or use a do-while pattern: call once, then check in a while loop.
tasks.walkthrough:
Everything about a single game moves inside `play_hangman()`. The word list stays outside since it doesn't change between games.
The loop at the bottom plays one game, asks, and either goes again or breaks.
Because each call to the function sets up fresh variables, every game starts clean.

tasks.description: Final polish: draw a simple ASCII hangman that updates with each wrong guess. Each wrong guess adds a body part to the drawing.
tasks.hint:
Create a list of ASCII art strings — one for each stage (0 wrong to 6 wrong).
Index into the list using the number of wrong guesses: `stages[wrong_count]`
Print the current stage at the start of each round.
tasks.solution:
import random

STAGES = [
    '''
      +---+
          |
          |
          |
     =======''',
    '''
      +---+
      O   |
          |
          |
     =======''',
    '''
      +---+
      O   |
      |   |
          |
     =======''',
    '''
      +---+
      O   |
     /|   |
          |
     =======''',
    '''
      +---+
      O   |
     /|\  |
          |
     =======''',
    '''
      +---+
      O   |
     /|\  |
     /    |
     =======''',
    '''
      +---+
      O   |
     /|\  |
     / \  |
     =======''',
]

words = {
    'animals': ['cat', 'dog', 'horse', 'rabbit'],
    'fruits': ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'],
    'languages': ['python', 'rust', 'kotlin'],
}

def play_hangman():
    category = random.choice(list(words.keys()))
    word = random.choice(words[category])
    guessed = set()
    wrong = []
    max_tries = len(STAGES) - 1

    def display():
        return ' '.join(c if c in guessed else '_' for c in word)

    def won():
        return all(c in guessed for c in word)

    print(f'Category: {category}')
    while not won() and len(wrong) < max_tries:
        print(STAGES[len(wrong)])
        print(display())
        print(f'Wrong: {wrong}')
        guess = input('Guess a letter: ').lower()
        if len(guess) != 1 or not guess.isalpha():
            print('Enter a single letter!')
            continue
        if guess in guessed:
            print('Already tried!')
            continue
        guessed.add(guess)
        if guess not in word:
            wrong.append(guess)

    print(STAGES[len(wrong)])
    if won():
        print(f'You won! The word was: {word}')
    else:
        print(f'Game over! The word was: {word}')

while True:
    play_hangman()
    if input('Play again? (y/n): ').lower() != 'y':
        break
tasks.walkthrough:
Seven drawings cover zero to six wrong guesses. Because they're in a list, `STAGES[len(wrong)]` picks the right one with no if statements.
`max_tries` is derived from the list length, so adding or removing a stage automatically adjusts the game.
The final drawing is printed once more after the loop so the player sees the finished figure on a loss.

lesson.intro:
Time to build Hangman from a blank editor, without the scaffolding of the last
two days. If you get stuck, the solutions from days 28 and 29 are still there.
Then you'll add categories, a play-again loop, and a drawing.

sections.heading: Planning before typing
sections.body:
Before writing any code, sketch the pieces in comments. Something like this.
Then fill in each comment with code and run after every step.
sections.code:
# 1. pick a random word
# 2. guessed = set(), wrong = [], max_tries = 6
# 3. while not won and tries left:
#       show blanks, ask for a letter, validate, update
# 4. print win or lose, reveal word

sections.heading: Categories with a dictionary
sections.body:
Store words under category names. Pick a random category with
`random.choice(list(words.keys()))`, then a random word from that
category's list. Tell the player the category as a clue.
sections.code:
import random

words = {'animals': ['cat', 'dog'], 'fruits': ['apple', 'pear']}
category = random.choice(list(words.keys()))
word = random.choice(words[category])
print(f'Category: {category}')
print(len(word))

sections.heading: Play again
sections.body:
Wrap the game in a function, then loop around it. The whole game becomes one
line inside the loop, which is why functions are worth the effort.

sections.heading: A drawing that grows
sections.body:
Put one drawing per stage in a list, index 0 for no wrong guesses up to
index 6 for the full figure. Then `stages[len(wrong)]` picks the right one.
Triple-quoted strings make multi-line art easy.

watch_out: Trying to write the whole game before running anything. Get the loop working with a fixed word first.
Reading the category without converting `.keys()` to a list. `random.choice` needs a sequence.
Off-by-one on the stages list: with 6 tries you need 7 drawings, from 0 wrong to 6 wrong.
